articles.title: A Sandbox Got Popped at Black Hat. Nobody Should Be Shocked.
articles.summary: The sandbox was never the point A researcher stood up at Black Hat USA 2026 and claimed C2-style control over ChatGPT's code execution sandbox. Zero points on HN. Zero comments. That gap between "someone got command-and-control on a major AI platform's isolation layer" and "total internet silence" tells you almost everything about where we are in the hype cycle right now. We're numb to this category of finding, and that numbness is the actual story. This isn't new, it's just wearing a new hat Sandbox escapes are one of the oldest genres in security research. Browser sandboxes, container runtimes, VM hypervisors, JVM security managers. Every isolation boundary humans have ever built has eventually leaked, because isolation is an assumption enforced by code, and code has bugs. articles.title: AI in Luxury Travel: Why Virtuoso Travel Advisors Who Use AI Will Replace Those Who Don’t
articles.summary: AI won’t replace luxury travel advisors, but advisors who use AI will have a competitive advantage over those who don’t. Virtuoso and the broader travel industry are moving toward AI-powered tools that can automate busywork, improve personalization, and turn traveler preferences into better recommendations.
